subject: english-literature
source_note: Structure follows the IB Diploma Language A: Literature guide (first assessment 2021): three areas of exploration studied across a body of literary works, assessed through Paper 1, Paper 2 and the individual oral. Area and component names are guide-accurate; connections, sequence and prerequisites are expert-authored teaching relationships (the IB does not publish these).

connections.why: Paper 1 rewards close analysis of authorial choices
Meaning emerges in the interaction of text and reader
Authorial choices create the aesthetic of literary language
Context of production shapes how a text is received
Context conditions how identity and society are represented
Meaning-making is deepened by reading texts in context
Texts that travel invite comparison across time and place
Paper 2 is a comparative essay across two works
Knowing movements supports comparison between texts
Recurring themes give comparative essays their focus
The oral connects works to a global issue and society
The oral analyses how authorial choices treat the issue
Paper 1 is the reader's own guided interpretation

Reception over time is shaped by literary movements
